castleford.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Castleford
s1loc: Castleford sits at the heart of the Five Towns, and its charity sector is busy. Trinity Mission, founded by Trinity Methodist Church, runs a drop-in food bank, soup kitchen and clothing bank, while the Foodbank at the Link at Smawthorne Community Church on Beancroft Road has fed local people since 2013. The big food-redistribution and foodbank networks back this work, and the Prince of Wales Hospice supplies the wider Five Towns area, so demand for practical, low-cost workwear runs right across the town all year round.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops on Carlton Street and across the district, with central buying and trade accounts, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Smawthorne, Airedale, Glasshoughton and Whitwood. We are glad to outfit the national charity ordering in bulk and the one-room foodbank alike, with proper trade accounts for the larger names and direct online ordering with no minimum for the smallest group.

There is real depth beyond the food banks. The Prince of Wales Hospice runs charity shops across the Five Towns, raising funds for palliative care, and Age UK Wakefield District has a charity-shop presence covering Castleford and Normanton. Knottingley Foodbank, run by volunteers, reaches into Castleford and Hemsworth, and the NOVA-supported voluntary sector links community projects across Wakefield district. Mutual-aid groups and warm spaces in Glasshoughton and Airedale lean on dependable, washable kit that keeps every spare pound going to the cause.

ilkeston.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Ilkeston
s1loc: Ilkeston sits in the borough of Erewash, and its charity sector is well established. Arena Community, a registered charity born in 2006, runs a food bank from its Community Hub on Belfield Street and last year helped over 5,000 people across Ilkeston and the surrounding area. Every One Eats delivers food parcels to homes and runs community meals, while the big food-redistribution and foodbank networks underpin the work. With Treetops Hospice rooted nearby, demand for affordable, hard-wearing workwear runs steadily through the town.

There is genuine depth here too. Treetops Hospice runs its Ilkeston charity shop and furniture store on South Street, raising funds for end-of-life care across Derbyshire and Nottinghamshire, with another shop in nearby Heanor. Arena Church on the same Community Hub site coordinates volunteers across the town, and Erewash Borough Council signposts food banks throughout the borough. Volunteer-run warm spaces and community projects across Cotmanhay and Kirk Hallam rely on washable, low-cost kit that puts donors' money where it matters most.

cramlington.s1_head: Charity and volunteer kit in Cramlington
s1loc: Cramlington has a strong, locally rooted charity scene. Cramlington Foodbank, an independent charity run by local trustees and volunteers and part of the wider foodbank network, has around 40 volunteers giving 260 hours a week. In 2024 it took in 38 tonnes of donations and issued food parcels feeding some 3,500 people. The Hope Centre runs it from the local church, and the big food-redistribution networks support the work, so demand for practical, budget-friendly workwear is constant across the town.

The sector here runs at every size. National and regional charities keep shops with central buying and trade accounts, while small community groups, foodbanks, pantries and volunteer-run projects work on a shoestring across Eastfield, Mayfield, Beaconhill and Collingwood. There is real breadth beyond food parcels. Cramlington Foodbank adds crafting days, listening groups and uniform banks, and hosts weekly Shelter housing-advice sessions. The Matthew Project reaches across Cramlington, Bedlington, Blyth, Choppington and Guidepost, while Wansbeck Valley Food Bank serves the wider belt. s1loc: Glenrothes has a well-organised voluntary sector. Glenrothes and District Foodbank, based at Caledonia House in the Saltire Centre, hands out three-day and seven-day parcels along with fuel vouchers, clothes, homeware and a cafe, and is backed by the wider food-redistribution and foodbank networks. Fife Voluntary Action, the third-sector body for Fife, runs an office in the town.
